claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort on day 0 and days 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis, showed that 594 genes changed significantly in at least one comparison versus day 0.

sources.quote: RNA samples obtained from whole blood of 15 YF17D-vaccinated individuals (from the Montreal cohort) on the day of vaccination (day 0) and at several time points after vaccination (day 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60) were amplified and hybridized onto Illumina chips and analyzed. Expression profiles of 594 genes (Supplemental document 1, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1) were found to change significantly between day 0 and any time point after vaccination (with P < 0.05 and fold change less than −1.3 or >1.3).

Figure 1. Vaccination with YF17D induces early gene modulation. Global view of gene modulation in total blood cells after YF17D vaccination, as analyzed by gene array on the Montreal cohort (n = 9–15, depending on the time point). Heat map representation (a) and PCA (b) using the significantly modulated genes, in at least one comparison versus day 0.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort on day 0 and days 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after vaccination, using heat map representation and principal component analysis, showed that gene expression modulation was greatest at days 3 and 7 among the measured post-vaccination timepoints.

sources.quote: The peak of modulation of gene expression, as shown by heat map representation (Fig. 1 a) and principal component analysis (Fig. 1 b), primarily occurred at days 3 and 7 after vaccination, whereas a limited number of significant genes were modulated in response to vaccination at day 10 after vaccination or beyond.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated human volunteers in the first week after vaccination, using independent component analysis followed by gene set enrichment, showed that IRF7, STAT1, and ETS2 were identified as transcription factors with predicted target genes that were significantly modulated between day 0 and day 7 in n = 11 volunteers.

sources.quote: Independent component analysis (ICA), followed by gene set enrichment, identified transcription factors with predicted (11) target genes showing a specific modulation after YF17D vaccination (Fig. 2 and Fig. S1, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1). With this approach, three major nodes of transcriptional regulation of downstream target genes were found as early as day 3 (IRF7 and STAT1) and day 7 (ETS2).

Figure 2. Transcriptional network of differentially expressed genes after YF17D vaccination, as inferred by gene set enrichment. Network representation of inferred transcription factors (11) and predicted target genes that are significantly modulated. Node colors indicate fold change of gene expression between day 0 and 7 in n = 11 volunteers.

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from YF17D-vaccinated human volunteers in the first week after vaccination, using independent component analysis followed by gene set enrichment, showed that IRF1, IRF8, GATA6, GATA1, TAL1, FOXO3a, E2F4, E2F1, LMO2, SRF, and CEBPB were identified as transcription factors controlling the expression of several genes and pathways that were significantly modulated between day 0 and day 7 in n = 11 volunteers.

sources.quote: Other nodes of transcription factors (IRF1, IRF8, GATA6, GATA1, TAL1, FOXO3a, E2F4, E2F1, LMO2, SRF, and CEBPB) also controlled the expression of several of the genes and pathways that were modulated in the first week after immunization.

Figure 2. Transcriptional network of differentially expressed genes after YF17D vaccination, as inferred by gene set enrichment. Network representation of inferred transcription factors (11) and predicted target genes that are significantly modulated. Node colors indicate fold change of gene expression between day 0 and 7 in n = 11 volunteers. IRF1, IRF8, and genes targeted by IRF1 or IRF8, but no other transcription factors in the figure were removed to increase readability (see Fig. S1 for a complete map).

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from the Montreal cohort of 20 volunteers after a single YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential-expression analysis, showed that 43 genes encoding ribosomal proteins were down-regulated early after vaccination compared to day 0.

sources.quote: Strikingly, we observed that 43 genes encoding ribosomal proteins were down-regulated in PBMCs early after vaccination with YF17D (Supplemental document 1), confirming the findings of a previous study (15).

claim_7.claim: qPCR analysis of RNA from independent YF17D vaccination trials in the Montreal cohort, Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers), and Emory cohort (10 volunteers), at day 0 and day 7 after vaccination, showed that most genes up-regulated in the Montreal cohort also had increased fold-change expression in the Lausanne and Emory cohorts compared to baseline.

sources.quote: The results illustrated in Fig. 4 and in Fig. S3 indicate that most genes that were up-regulated in the Montreal cohort also showed increased expression in the two other independent trials.
Figure 4. Heat map of fold change gene expression between day 0 and 7, as measured by qPCR. For a complete heat map of all measured fold changes see Fig. S3.

claim_8.claim: qPCR analysis of RNA from independent YF17D vaccination trials in the Montreal cohort, Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers), and Emory cohort (10 volunteers), at day 0 and day 7 after vaccination, showed that most genes down-regulated in the Montreal cohort also had decreased fold-change expression in the Lausanne and Emory cohorts compared to baseline.

sources.quote: Conversely, most down-regulated genes in the Montreal cohort also showed decreased levels of expression in the samples obtained from the two other trials.
Figure 4. Heat map of fold change gene expression between day 0 and 7, as measured by qPCR. For a complete heat map of all measured fold changes see Fig. S3.

claim_9.claim: Microarray analysis of whole-blood RNA from the Montreal cohort (20 volunteers) at day 3 after YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis and heat-map display of up-regulation, showed that CASP1 and CASP5 mRNA were up-regulated compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: Our gene array results showed that two components of the inflammasome, caspase-1 and -5, were up-regulated at the mRNA level in the Montreal cohort, 3 d after vaccination with YF17D (Fig. 5 a).

Figure 5. YF17D induces expression of genes associated with IL-1β and activates the inflammasome. (a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β–associated genes.

claim_10.claim: Microarray analysis of whole-blood RNA from the Montreal cohort (20 volunteers) at an unspecified post-vaccination timepoint after YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis, probe-level consideration restricted to probes targeting all transcripts for IL-1R2 and IL-1RN, and heat-map display of modulation, showed that IL-1R2 and IL-1RN mRNA were modulated compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: Two other genes related to IL-1β production and signaling that were modulated by the vaccine are IL-1R2 and -1RN.

(a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β–associated genes. For IL-1R2 and -1RN only probes targeting all transcripts were considered.

claim_11.claim: Microarray analysis of whole-blood RNA from the Lausanne cohort (13 volunteers) at an unspecified post-vaccination timepoint after YF17D vaccination, using LIMMA differential expression analysis, probe-level consideration restricted to probes targeting all transcripts for IL-1R2 and IL-1RN, and heat-map display of modulation, showed that CASP1, IL-1R2, and IL-1RN mRNA were similarly modulated compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: All of these genes, except for caspase-5, were also similarly modulated in the Lausanne cohort.

(a) Heat maps showing the up-regulation of genes encoding inflammasome components and the modulation of other, IL-1β–associated genes. For IL-1R2 and -1RN only probes targeting all transcripts were considered.

claim_12.claim: ELISA analysis of monocyte-derived DC supernatants from monocyte-derived DCs incubated with live (YF) or UV-inactivated (UV) YF17D, using IL-1β quantification, showed that IL-1β secretion increased compared to noninfected cells (NI).

sources.quote: The results show that DCs incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D showed a marked increased IL-1β secretion (up to ninefold, compared with DCs incubated in medium alone), whereas heat-inactivated YF17D only triggered a modest secretion of the proinflammatory cytokine (Fig. 5 b and Fig. S4, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1).

(b) IL-1β production by monocyte-derived DCs incubated with live (YF), UV-inactivated (UV), or heat-inactivated (HI) YF17D, as determined by ELISA. NI, noninfected cells. This represents the results from one representative of three separate experiments. The results for the two other experiments are shown in Fig. S4.

claim_14.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from six selected YF17D-vaccinated volunteers at day 60 after vaccination, using CFSE labeling, showed that both CD4+ and CD8+ T cell proliferative responses were highly variable among the vaccinated volunteers.

sources.quote: Both the CD4+ and CD8+ T cell proliferative responses were highly variable among the vaccinated volunteers.

(a) Day 60 PBMCs were stimulated with the 22 peptide pools and assayed by CFSE labeling for their proliferative response. Bar graphs show data for six selected volunteers, and the dataset for all the volunteers can be found in Fig. S6 (c and d).

claim_15.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from six selected YF17D-vaccinated volunteers at day 60 after vaccination, using CFSE labeling, showed that CD8+ T cell proliferative responses were generally much weaker than CD4+ T cell proliferative responses in the same vaccinated volunteers.

sources.quote: The CD8+ responses were generally much weaker than those observed in CD4+ T cells

(a) Day 60 PBMCs were stimulated with the 22 peptide pools and assayed by CFSE labeling for their proliferative response. Bar graphs show data for six selected volunteers, and the dataset for all the volunteers can be found in Fig. S6 (c and d).

claim_16.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from YF17D-vaccinated volunteers after immunization, using CFSE labeling, showed that both CD4+ and CD8+ T cell peptide-specific memory proliferative responses to the most immunodominant peptide pools were detected as long as 1 yr after immunization (day 365).

sources.quote: Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cell peptide-specific responses were persistent, as memory proliferative responses to the most immunodominant peptide pools were detected as long as 1 yr after immunization
these results show that the breadth of the T cell responses to the YF17D vaccine is highly variable from one vaccinated individual to another, but that those responses are persistent.

claim_17.claim: Cytometric bead assay analysis of PBMCs supernatants from six selected YF17D-vaccinated volunteers at 24 h of culture after stimulation with YF17D-derived 22 peptide pools showed that TNF was detected at high levels whereas IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-10 were found in low amounts or not detected in the same samples.

sources.quote: In our system, high levels of TNF were detected in several supernatants, whereas the other cytokines were either found in low amounts or not detected.
At 24 h of culture, supernatants were analyzed by CBA to determine the Th1/Th2 cytokine secretion profile in response to each pool. The heat maps represent the data for the same six volunteers.

claim_18.claim: Cytometric bead assay analysis of PBMCs supernatants from six selected YF17D-vaccinated volunteers at 24 h of culture after stimulation with YF17D-derived 22 peptide pools showed that the qualitative and quantitative features of cytokine production were highly variable among vaccinated volunteers.

sources.quote: Hence, the qualitative and quantitative features of cytokine production were highly variable

claim_19.claim: Cytometric bead assay analysis of PBMCs supernatants from vaccinated volunteers after stimulation with YF17D-derived peptide pools showed that both Th1 and Th2 cytokine secretion profiles were induced in most volunteers (12 out of 15).

sources.quote: In most volunteers (12 out of 15), both Th1 and Th2 cytokine secretion profiles were induced by YF17D peptide pools.

claim_20.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from YF17D-vaccinated volunteers at day 365 after vaccination, using stimulation with immunostimulatory YF17D peptide pools and restimulation or not with the same peptide pools before staining, showed that both Th1 and Th2 central memory CD4+ T cells expressing CD154 could be detected over background (S) in the RS samples in all four volunteers tested.

sources.quote: To determine if this mixed Th1/Th2 response was persistent, we detected YF17D-specific Th1 and Th2 cells in PBMCs sampled at day 365 after vaccination.
However, both Th1 and Th2 central memory T cells could be detected in all four volunteers tested.

(b) FACS analysis of PBMCs from day 365 after vaccination. Cells from four volunteers were stimulated (S) for with immunostimulatory YF17D peptide pools, and then restimulated (RS) or not with the same peptide pools before staining. The data were analyzed according to the gating strategy shown in Fig. S7, and are expressed as the percentage of central memory CD4+ T cells (CD45RA2CCR7+) that express the marker for recent activation CD154, and that are either Th1 or Th2 in the RS samples, over background (S).

claim_21.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of DC/T cell co-cultures from YF-naive individuals after 14 d co-culture, using short restimulation with autologous DC targets left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D, showed that live or UV-inactivated YF17D-pulsed DCs primed a strong antigen-specific response with CD154 and IFN-γ expression in live CD4+-gated events compared to untouched autologous DC targets.

sources.quote: As shown in Fig. 8 a, DCs pulsed with YF17D virus (live or UV-inactivated) primed a strong antigen-specific response of naive T cells, with up to 4% cells expressing CD154 and IFN-γ in response to live or UV-inactivated YF17D.

(a and b) Purified T helper cells were mixed with DCs that had been incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D. After 14 d, the cells were harvested and evaluated by flow cytometry for cytokine and CD154 expression after a short restimulation with autologous DCs targets that had been left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D. All data plots show live CD4+-gated events. These are representative data of experiments done on cells from at least 10 volunteers.

claim_22.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of DC/T cell co-cultures from YF-naive individuals after 14 d co-culture, using short restimulation with autologous DC targets left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D, showed that YF17D-pulsed DCs stimulated antigen-specific Th2 cells expressing IL-5 and IL-13 in live CD4+-gated events compared to untouched autologous DC targets.

sources.quote: Similarly, YF17D-pulsed DCs stimulated high numbers of antigen-specific Th2 cells expressing IL-5 and IL-13, upon restimulation with live or inactivated virus (Fig. 8 b).

(a and b) Purified T helper cells were mixed with DCs that had been incubated with live or UV-inactivated YF17D. After 14 d, the cells were harvested and evaluated by flow cytometry for cytokine and CD154 expression after a short restimulation with autologous DCs targets that had been left untouched, pulsed with killed YF17D, or infected with live YF17D. All data plots show live CD4+-gated events. These are representative data of experiments done on cells from at least 10 volunteers.

claim_23.claim: Multiplex cytokine analysis of culture supernatants from YF-naive individuals after 14 d DC/T cell co-culture showed that IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-13, and IL-5 levels were high when YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen compared to co-cultures with no recall antigen.

sources.quote: When YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen, the cells produced high levels of all the cytokines measured except IL-10, compared with co-cultures with no recall antigen.
(c) Alternatively, the culture supernatants were harvested and evaluated by a multiplex cytokine analysis. Data representative of experiments done on cells from two volunteers.

claim_24.claim: Multiplex cytokine analysis of culture supernatants from YF-naive individuals after 14 d DC/T cell co-culture showed that IL-10 was not produced at high levels when YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen compared to co-cultures with no recall antigen.

sources.quote: When YF17D was used as pulse and recall antigen, the cells produced high levels of all the cytokines measured except IL-10, compared with co-cultures with no recall antigen.
(c) Alternatively, the culture supernatants were harvested and evaluated by a multiplex cytokine analysis. Data representative of experiments done on cells from two volunteers.

claim_25.claim: Microarray analysis of total RNA from co-cultures containing YF17D-pulsed DCs and CD4+ T cells from normal healthy donors in the VaxDesign MIMIC system, using independent component analysis and gene set enrichment, showed that eight transcriptional nodes were consistently identified in day 7 versus day 0 antigen-response gene modulation: ETS2, STAT1, IRF1, IRF7, IRF8, GATA1, LMO2, and JUN.

sources.quote: Co-cultures containing YF17D-pulsed DCs and CD4+ T cells (with or without YF17D as recall antigen) were harvested and total RNA was isolated from the cells. Gene modulation in response to the antigen (day 7 vs. 0) was assessed by microarray analysis. In total, eight nodes of transcriptional regulation of downstream target genes were consistently identified; ETS2, STAT1, IRF1, IRF7, IRF8, GATA1, LMO2, and JUN (Fig. 9).

Figure 9. Consensus transcriptional network of genes differentially expressed on day 7 as compared with day 0. Network representation of inferred transcription factors and predicted target genes that are consistently modulated in at least two out of three datasets, with the third dataset not being contradictory.
